The presence of multiple targets for Theasaponin E1, including both organic anion transporters and phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate 3-kinase subunits, suggests a broader role in cellular signaling. The integrated evidence supports a mechanism where K-252a may act as a modulator or inhibitor of Theasaponin E1, thereby influencing the activity of the kinase. The observed scores and the shared targets across the paths provide a robust foundation for this relationship, though further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the exact nature of the interaction.
